title: Create claude-workers namespace and secrets manifest
description: Create the Kubernetes namespace and a Secret template for credentials needed by worker pods.
acceptance_criteria: `kubectl apply -f agents/namespace.yaml` creates the `claude-workers` namespace
`agents/secrets.yaml.example` exists and documents all required fields: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`
`agents/secrets.yaml` is listed in `.gitignore` so actual credentials are never committed
README explains how to apply the real secret manually

title: Build claude-worker base Dockerfile
description:
Create the base container image that all worker pods will use. It should include Claude Code CLI, tmux, git, GitHub CLI, jq, and the user's dotfiles from github.com/kfoxb/dotfiles.

Base from `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:bullseye`. Install Node.js 20 via nodesource or nvm. Install `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` globally via npm. Create non-root user `claude` with sudo. Clone and run dotfiles install at build time.
acceptance_criteria: Image builds successfully without errors
Running `claude --version` inside the container works
Running `tmux -V`, `git --version`, `gh --version`, `jq --version` all work
Dotfiles directory is present in the `claude` user's home directory
Container runs as non-root user `claude` by default

title: Write pod entrypoint script
description:
Write `entrypoint.sh` that runs when a worker pod starts. It orchestrates the full Claude Code session lifecycle.

Steps:
1. Configure git credential store from `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var (write to `~/.git-credentials`)
2. Clone `$REPO_URL` into `/workspace/`
3. Checkout `$GIT_BRANCH`; if branch doesn't exist remotely, create it from the default branch
4. Start a tmux session named `claude` running Claude Code in headless mode: `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json 2>&1 | tee /workspace/.claude-output.log`
5. Background monitor: poll for tmux session exit, write `/tmp/claude-done` with exit code, use `kubectl label` to update pod status label to `done` or `error`
6. Keep container alive: `wait` or `tail -f /dev/null` so pod doesn't exit after Claude finishes
7. Handle `SIGTERM` gracefully: send SIGTERM to Claude process, wait for it to finish, then exit
acceptance_criteria: Pod starts and git clone completes successfully for a test repo
Claude Code runs inside a tmux session named `claude`
`kubectl exec -it <pod> -- tmux attach -t claude` attaches to the session
Container stays alive after Claude finishes
Pod label `status` changes to `done` when Claude exits cleanly
Pod label `status` changes to `error` when Claude exits with non-zero code
SIGTERM causes graceful shutdown within 30 seconds

title: Create pod manifest template
description:
Create a Kubernetes Pod manifest template that is parameterized via environment variables and `envsubst`.

Required env vars for substitution: `TASK_NAME`, `REPO_URL`, `REPO_SLUG`, `GIT_BRANCH`, `LINEAR_TICKET`.

The manifest should:
- Use the base claude-worker image
- Set namespace `claude-workers`
- Include labels: `app=claude-worker`, `task`, `repo`, `branch`, `ticket`, `status=running`
- Reference the `claude-worker-secrets` Secret for env vars
- Set resource requests/limits (cpu: 500m/2000m, memory: 1Gi/4Gi)
- Use the `claude-worker` ServiceAccount (from rbac.yaml)
- Mount an `emptyDir` at `/workspace`
acceptance_criteria: `envsubst < agents/pod-template.yaml | kubectl apply -f -` creates a pod in `claude-workers`
All required labels are present on the created pod
Pod has correct resource limits
Secrets are mounted as environment variables
Workspace emptyDir is mounted at /workspace

title: Build and push base image (manual process)
description:
Create a build script that builds the base image and pushes it to a registry. For Phase 1 this is a manual process — the in-cluster registry isn't set up until Phase 5, so push to ghcr.io.

The script should:
- Build the Dockerfile with a `latest` tag and a SHA-based tag
- Push both tags
- Document the required `docker login` for ghcr.io
- Note that in Phase 5 this will be updated to also push to the local in-cluster registry
acceptance_criteria: `bash agents/base-image/build.sh` builds and pushes the image without errors
Image is available at `ghcr.io/<org>/claude-worker:latest`
README documents the one-time setup (docker login, GITHUB_TOKEN for ghcr.io)

title: Create RBAC for pod self-labeling
description:
Worker pods need to update their own labels to reflect current status (running, done, error, rate-limited). Create a ServiceAccount with a Role that allows patching pods in the `claude-workers` namespace.

The entrypoint script uses `kubectl label pod $HOSTNAME <label>=<value>` to update status. For this to work without a kubeconfig file, the pod's ServiceAccount token (auto-mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/) must have patch permissions on pods.

Create:
- ServiceAccount `claude-worker` in `claude-workers` namespace
- Role `claude-worker` with `patch` on `pods` resource
- RoleBinding binding the ServiceAccount to the Role
acceptance_criteria: `kubectl apply -f agents/rbac.yaml` creates ServiceAccount, Role, and RoleBinding
A pod running as the `claude-worker` ServiceAccount can run `kubectl label pod $HOSTNAME status=done` without error
The pod-template.yaml references `serviceAccountName: claude-worker`
